With the proliferation of personal data collection and the increasing interconnectedness of our lives through various digital platforms, ensuring and maintaining privacy has become more challenging but also more critical.

It allows us to navigate our lives without constant surveillance, make decisions without fear of reprisal, and express ourselves freely. The right to privacy also protects us from unfair, selective, or prejudiced treatment by those in power.

Privacy is crucial to our democratic values, too. It allows everyone to participate fully in society without the fear of judgment or discrimination based on their most personal or sensitive information. With the rise of mass surveillance and targeted advertising, all societies must decide how they value privacy and security: the former often coming at the expense of the other.
